citeAs: Masry, A., Long, D. X., Tan, J. Q., Joty, S., & Hoque, E. (2022). ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning. arXiv preprint arXiv:2203.10244.
creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque (York University, Nanyang Technological University, Salesforce Research)
description: A large-scale benchmark covering 9.6K human-written questions as well as 23.1K questions generated from human-written chart summaries for question answering about charts with visual and logical reasoning.
name: ChartQA
rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers with an acceptance rate of 95% and total accomplished HITs of 5000. Compensated based on the US minimum wage ($7.25 USD per hour).
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Overall agreement between crowd workers based on exact matches was 61.04%. Manual checking on 500 random samples showed 78.55% agreement when considering typos and lexical variations.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Workers were asked to focus on compositional and visual questions. For each chart, workers provided two questions with answers. The same questions were then answered by another annotator. If answers exactly matched, it was considered correct; otherwise, answers were manually checked to select the final correct answer.
rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four online sources: Statista, Pew research, Our World In Data (OWID), and OECD. Underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and associated text descriptions were extracted where available.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: 20,882 real-world charts curated from four online sources (Statista, Pew research, Our World In Data, OECD) covering diverse visual styles and topics like economy, politics, and industry.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataLimitations: The T5 question generation model may generate invalid, incomplete, or unanswerable questions due to domain mismatch. Also, automatic data extraction from charts is error-prone.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Dataset augmentation was performed by fine-tuning a T5 model on SQuAD to automatically generate 23.1K questions from human-written chart summaries.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Generated questions were filtered using a heuristic that removes questions if the answer cannot be found in the chart data table. The test set of the machine-generated dataset was manually cleaned by removing invalid questions.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors note that their models can be abused to mislead the public about the charts' content and implications.
rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating Chart Question Answering (ChartQA) systems that take a chart and a natural language question as input and predict the answer.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: A pre-trained T5 model fine-tuned on the SQuAD QA dataset was used to automatically generate questions from human-written chart summaries.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: To protect the privacy of the annotators, all of their annotations were anonymized.
